title: What do others really think?
hook: Would correcting a mistaken social belief change a household's choice?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish private support from beliefs about others' support and the measured downstream action.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish private support from beliefs about others' support and the measured downstream action.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy survey, private support is 80%, while the perceived support of others is 40%. What is the underestimation? Toy inputs A=[80, 40]; B=[80, 75].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[40, 80, 40], [5, 80, 75]]. Labels: Belief error pp, Private %, Perceived %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Private attitudes and beliefs about other people’s attitudes are separate quantities. The comparison changes the belief estimate while holding private support fixed. Any downstream application or employment effect requires an additional outcome measure.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Private support %=80, Perceived support %=75. What is Belief error pp? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Private support %=80, Perceived support %=75. What is Belief error pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Most Saudi men privately supported women working outside the home but underestimated others' support; correcting this raised wives' job applications (Bursztyn, González & Yanagizawa-Drott, 2020).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish private support from beliefs about others' support and the measured downstream action.
